title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 1.5 Relationships within the Family

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Healthy family relationships keep children safe and teach them to respect one another. In this sub-strand you will learn to be careful when you are alone with someone, how to protect yourself from sexual abuse, and whom to tell if anyone touches you in a bad way. You will read 1 Corinthians 6:19 and 2 Samuel 13:4-14 and treat your body as the temple of the Holy Spirit.

## Strand 1.0: Creation
Sub-strand 1.5: Relationships within the Family
Suggested lessons: 3

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 1.0 Creation, Sub-strand 1.5 Relationships within the Family
• 2 Samuel 13:4-14; 1 Corinthians 6:19

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) take care when alone with people of the opposite sex
b) mention ways of protecting oneself from sexual abuse
c) identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused
d) appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why are healthy family relationships important?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• sing a song related to respecting their bodies as the temple of the Holy Spirit
• in turns, read 2 Samuel 13:4-14
• say whom to report to if they are touched inappropriately or sexually abused
• in groups, tell how they should protect themselves from sexual abuse
• role-play ways of protecting themselves from sexual abuse
• write 1 Corinthians 6:19 on flash cards and meditate on it
• watch a video clip of children being tempted with gifts, but they say NO! to the strangers

## Core competencies
• Collaboration: the skill of team work is portrayed as learners carry out activities in groups.
• Digital literacy: the skill of digital citizenship is enhanced as learners act safely and responsibly while watching video clips.
• Self-Efficacy: the skill of expressing their needs clearly for help is nurtured as they say whom to report to if they are touched inappropriately or sexually abused.

## Values
• Unity: learners collaborate with each other as they read the Bible in turns.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Gender awareness: is nurtured as they learn how to protect themselves from sexual abuse.
• Human Sexuality-Abstinence: learners acquire the virtue of holiness as they say no to inappropriate touching or report cases of sexual abuse

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing songs and write poems.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: Being careful when you are alone

LESSON 1: BEING CAREFUL WHEN YOU ARE ALONE
==========================================

## What you will learn
• Tell the story of Tamar and Amnon in 2 Samuel 13:4-14 in a safe, simple way.
• State how to take care when alone with people of the opposite sex.

Curriculum outcomes: a) take care when alone with people of the opposite sex

## Introduction
Most family members love and protect children. The Bible also tells a sad story of a brother who used a trick and would not listen when a girl said no. That story teaches you to be careful.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: Being careful when you are alone — The story in 2 Samuel 13:4-14

## Notes

### The story in 2 Samuel 13:4-14
Amnon was a son of King David. He told his friend Jonadab that he wanted Tamar, the sister of Absalom, in a wrong way. Jonadab told him to pretend to be ill and to ask the king to send Tamar to prepare food for him. King David sent Tamar to Amnon's house.

Tamar made the food. Amnon refused to eat it while other people were there and sent them out. He told Tamar to bring the food into his bedroom. Then he took hold of her and asked her to lie with him.

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: Being careful when you are alone — What the story teaches

Tamar said no. She told him not to force her. She said such a thing was wicked in Israel, and she asked him to speak to the king instead of doing this shameful act. Amnon would not listen to her. He was stronger than she was, and he forced her. That was sexual abuse. The wrong belonged to Amnon, not to Tamar. She had said no.

### What the story teaches
- Do not go into a closed room alone with someone who wants you there for a wrong reason.
- A relative can do wrong. Being in the family does not make a bad touch acceptable.
- Saying no is the right action, even if the other person is older or stronger.
- Pretending to be sick, or sending everyone else away, can be a trick. Notice it and leave.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: Being careful when you are alone — Taking care with the opposite sex

### Taking care with the opposite sex
Boys and girls can be friends, classmates and family. Take care when you are alone together. Stay where other people can see you. Do not lie on a bed with someone. Do not play games that involve undressing or secret touching. If a person of the opposite sex asks you to keep a meeting secret from your parents, do not go. Healthy families do not ask children to hide wrong actions.

## Key words
• opposite sex — a boy in relation to a girl, or a girl in relation to a boy
• sexual abuse — forcing or tricking someone into sexual touching or a sexual act
• inappropriate — not right or not acceptable

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: Being careful when you are alone — Read 2 Samuel 13:4-14 in turns

## Activity: Read 2 Samuel 13:4-14 in turns
You will need: Bible, Exercise book

1. In turns, read 2 Samuel 13:4-14. The teacher guides the reading so that it stays respectful.

2. As a class, retell only what the verses say: the trick, Tamar's refusal, and Amnon's refusal to listen.

3. List two ways to take care when you are alone with a person of the opposite sex.

4. Sing a song about respecting your body.

## Practice

1. How did Amnon get Tamar to come to him?

2. What did Tamar say when Amnon wanted to lie with her?

3. Give two ways to take care when you are alone with a person of the opposite sex.

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: Being careful when you are alone — Answers to practice

## Answers to practice

1. He pretended to be ill, and King David sent Tamar to prepare food for him.

2. She said no, told him not to force her, and said the act was wicked.

3. Any two: stay where others can see you; do not go into a closed bedroom; do not keep secret meetings; leave if everyone else is sent out; say no to bad touching.

## Summary
• Amnon tricked Tamar into a room alone and refused to listen when she said no.
• The wrong was his. Saying no was right.
• Stay where others can see you, and do not keep secret meetings.

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: Protecting yourself from sexual abuse

LESSON 2: PROTECTING YOURSELF FROM SEXUAL ABUSE
===============================================

## What you will learn
• Mention ways of protecting oneself from sexual abuse.
• Say no firmly to gifts or touches that are wrong.

Curriculum outcomes: b) mention ways of protecting oneself from sexual abuse

## Introduction
Your body belongs to you, and it belongs to God. Nobody is allowed to touch the private parts of your body or to ask you for sexual acts. You can learn ways to protect yourself.

## Notes

Sexual abuse is any sexual touching or sexual act that is forced, tricked or done to a child. A child cannot agree to it. It is always wrong, whether the person is a stranger, a neighbour, a worker at school, or a member of the family.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: Protecting yourself from sexual abuse — Ways to protect yourself

### Ways to protect yourself
- Say "No!" in a strong voice.
- Move away at once to a place with other people.
- Do not accept gifts, money, sweets or lifts from someone who wants a secret in return.
- Do not go to lonely places with anyone who makes you uneasy.
- Walk to school and back with other learners when you can.
- Do not watch or share bad pictures.
- Tell a parent or teacher if someone's words or touches make you uncomfortable.
- Refuse to keep a bad secret. A good secret is a surprise gift. A bad secret hides harm.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: Protecting yourself from sexual abuse — Gifts that are traps

### Gifts that are traps
Some people tempt children with gifts and then ask for wrong touching. You may like the gift and still say no. In a role-play, one learner offers a gift and says, "Do not tell anyone." The other learner says, "No! I will tell my parent." Then the learner walks away. Practise until the word No feels strong.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: Protecting yourself from sexual abuse — Your body is not the problem

### Your body is not the problem
Wearing a school uniform, being friendly, or being alone does not cause abuse. The person who touches wrongly is the one who sins. Protecting yourself is wisdom. It is the same wisdom Tamar showed when she refused, even though Amnon did not stop. You add another step she needed: run to a trusted adult as fast as you can.

## Key words
• protect — to keep yourself safe from harm
• bad secret — a secret that hides harm and should be told to a trusted adult
• private parts — the parts of the body covered by underwear, which others must not touch

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: Protecting yourself from sexual abuse — Role-play saying NO

## Activity: Role-play saying NO
You will need: Space to act

1. In groups, tell how you should protect yourselves from sexual abuse.

2. Role-play a child being tempted with a gift by someone who wants a secret. The child says NO and walks away.

3. Watch, if the teacher provides it, a video clip of children who are tempted with gifts but say NO to strangers.

4. Write two protection rules in your exercise book.

PAGE 15: Lesson 2: Protecting yourself from sexual abuse — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. What is sexual abuse?

2. List three ways to protect yourself from sexual abuse.

3. Why should you refuse a gift that comes with the words "Do not tell anyone"?

## Answers to practice

1. Forcing, tricking or involving a child in sexual touching or a sexual act. It is always wrong.

2. Any three: say No, move to where people are, refuse gifts that come with secrets, avoid lonely places, walk with friends, do not keep bad secrets, tell a trusted adult.

3. That kind of gift can be a trap leading to harm. A bad secret should be told to a trusted adult.

## Summary
• Sexual abuse is always wrong, even if the person is a relative.
• Say No, move away, refuse secret gifts, and do not keep bad secrets.
• The person who does the wrong touching is the one who sins.

PAGE 16: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple

LESSON 3: WHOM TO TELL, AND THE BODY AS GOD'S TEMPLE
====================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused.
• Explain 1 Corinthians 6:19 and choose to live a holy life.

Curriculum outcomes: c) identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused; d) appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life

## Introduction
If someone touches you in a way that feels wrong, you need a person who will believe you and help you. God also calls your body His temple. That is a reason to live a holy life.

PAGE 17: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Whom to report to

## Notes

### Whom to report to
If you are touched inappropriately or sexually abused, tell a person who can protect you:

- A parent or guardian
- A grandparent you trust
- Your class teacher or the head teacher
- A church leader or Sunday school teacher
- A police officer
- Another adult your parents have told you is safe

If the first person does not help, tell a second person. Keep telling until someone acts. In Kenya, a child can also call Childline Kenya on 116, free of charge. You can call the police on 999 or 112.

Report even if the person is a relative, even if you accepted a gift, and even if you were told to keep it secret. You will not be in trouble for telling. The abuse is not your fault.

PAGE 18: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Living a holy life

### 1 Corinthians 6:19
The verse says that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, and that you are not your own. A temple is a holy place where God is honoured. Write this verse on a flash card and meditate on it. Meditate means to think about it quietly and let it shape you.

### Living a holy life
Because the Holy Spirit dwells in Christians, we keep our bodies for God's honour.

- We say no to sexual sin and to sex before marriage.
- We dress neatly and respect other people's bodies.
- We do not use our bodies to harm or to shame anyone.
- We pray and ask God for strength to stay pure.

Appreciating the body as God's temple means thanking Him for it and refusing to let anyone treat it as a toy. Sing a song about respecting your body as the temple of the Holy Spirit.

PAGE 19: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Flash cards and people we report to

## Key words
• report — to tell a responsible person what happened
• temple of the Holy Spirit — the believer's body, where the Holy Spirit lives
• holy — set apart for God and kept pure

## Activity: Flash cards and people we report to
You will need: Flash cards, Bible, Pens

1. Each learner says whom he or she would report to if touched inappropriately.

2. Write 1 Corinthians 6:19 on a flash card and read it slowly, then sit quietly and think about it.

3. In groups, list ways to live a holy life.

4. Sing a song about the body as the temple of the Holy Spirit.

PAGE 20: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Practice

## Practice

1. Name three people you can report to if someone touches you inappropriately.

2. What number can a child in Kenya call free of charge for help?

3. What does 1 Corinthians 6:19 say about the body of a Christian?

## Answers to practice

1. Any three: a parent or guardian, a trusted grandparent, a teacher, a church leader, a police officer.

2. 116, Childline Kenya.

3. It is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and we are not our own.

## Summary
• Report bad touching to a parent, teacher, church leader or the police, and keep telling until you get help.
• Childline Kenya is 116.
• 1 Corinthians 6:19: your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, so live a holy life.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. In 2 Samuel 13, how did Amnon arrange for Tamar to come to him?
   A. He met her at the market
   B. He pretended to be ill so she would be sent to prepare food
   C. He wrote her a letter from another country
   D. He asked her in front of the whole town

2. What did Tamar do when Amnon asked her to lie with him?
   A. She agreed at once
   B. She said no and told him not to force her
   C. She called for a celebration
   D. She left the country before he spoke

3. Which action helps you take care when you are with a person of the opposite sex?
   A. Going into a closed bedroom alone
   B. Keeping the meeting secret from parents
   C. Staying where other people can see you
   D. Sending everyone else out of the room

4. Sexual abuse is...
   A. sometimes acceptable if the person is a relative
   B. always wrong
   C. the child's fault
   D. a game children should keep secret

5. Which of these protects you from sexual abuse?
   A. Accepting secret gifts
   B. Saying No and moving to where people are
   C. Keeping a bad secret
   D. Going to a lonely place

6. A bad secret is a secret that...

7. If someone touches you inappropriately, you should first:
   A. keep quiet forever
   B. tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher
   C. blame yourself
   D. hide from every adult

8. Which number is Childline Kenya?
   A. 116
   B. 100
   C. 123
   D. 911 only

9. 1 Corinthians 6:19 teaches that a Christian's body is:
   A. of no value
   B. a temple of the Holy Spirit
   C. belonging only to friends
   D. something to hide in shame

10. How can a learner live a holy life?

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. B. He pretended to be ill so she would be sent to prepare food
   Jonadab's plan was that Amnon should pretend to be ill and ask for Tamar to bring food.

2. B. She said no and told him not to force her
   Tamar refused and said the act was wicked. Amnon would not listen.

3. C. Staying where other people can see you
   Staying in view of other people is a way of taking care.

4. B. always wrong
   Sexual abuse is always wrong, and the blame belongs to the person who does it.

5. B. Saying No and moving to where people are
   A firm No and moving to other people are ways of protection.

6. hides harm and should be told to a trusted adult.
   Surprise gifts can be good secrets. Secrets about bad touching are not.

7. B. tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher
   Reporting to a responsible person brings help.

8. A. 116
   Children in Kenya can call 116 free of charge.

9. B. a temple of the Holy Spirit
   The verse says the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit and that we are not our own.

10. By saying no to sexual sin, respecting his or her body and other people's bodies, and asking God for help to stay pure.
   Holiness means being set apart for God, including keeping the body pure.

3. Why should you refuse a gift that comes with the words "Do not tell anyone"?

## Answers to practice

1. Forcing, tricking or involving a child in sexual touching or a sexual act. It is always wrong.

2. Any three: say No, move to where people are, refuse gifts that come with secrets, avoid lonely places, walk with friends, do not keep bad secrets, tell a trusted adult.

3. That kind of gift can be a trap leading to harm. A bad secret should be told to a trusted adult.

## Summary
• Sexual abuse is always wrong, even if the person is a relative.
• Say No, move away, refuse secret gifts, and do not keep bad secrets.
• The person who does the wrong touching is the one who sins.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple
studyPages.body:
LESSON 3: WHOM TO TELL, AND THE BODY AS GOD'S TEMPLE
====================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused.
• Explain 1 Corinthians 6:19 and choose to live a holy life.

Curriculum outcomes: c) identify whom to report to if touched inappropriately or sexually abused; d) appreciate the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit and live a holy life

## Introduction
If someone touches you in a way that feels wrong, you need a person who will believe you and help you. God also calls your body His temple. That is a reason to live a holy life.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Whom to report to
studyPages.body:
## Notes

### Whom to report to
If you are touched inappropriately or sexually abused, tell a person who can protect you:

- A parent or guardian
- A grandparent you trust
- Your class teacher or the head teacher
- A church leader or Sunday school teacher
- A police officer
- Another adult your parents have told you is safe

If the first person does not help, tell a second person. Keep telling until someone acts. In Kenya, a child can also call Childline Kenya on 116, free of charge. You can call the police on 999 or 112.

Report even if the person is a relative, even if you accepted a gift, and even if you were told to keep it secret. You will not be in trouble for telling. The abuse is not your fault.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Living a holy life
studyPages.body:
### 1 Corinthians 6:19
The verse says that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, and that you are not your own. A temple is a holy place where God is honoured. Write this verse on a flash card and meditate on it. Meditate means to think about it quietly and let it shape you.

### Living a holy life
Because the Holy Spirit dwells in Christians, we keep our bodies for God's honour.

- We say no to sexual sin and to sex before marriage.
- We dress neatly and respect other people's bodies.
- We do not use our bodies to harm or to shame anyone.
- We pray and ask God for strength to stay pure.

Appreciating the body as God's temple means thanking Him for it and refusing to let anyone treat it as a toy. Sing a song about respecting your body as the temple of the Holy Spirit.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Flash cards and people we report to
studyPages.body:
## Key words
• report — to tell a responsible person what happened
• temple of the Holy Spirit — the believer's body, where the Holy Spirit lives
• holy — set apart for God and kept pure

## Activity: Flash cards and people we report to
You will need: Flash cards, Bible, Pens

1. Each learner says whom he or she would report to if touched inappropriately.

2. Write 1 Corinthians 6:19 on a flash card and read it slowly, then sit quietly and think about it.

3. In groups, list ways to live a holy life.

4. Sing a song about the body as the temple of the Holy Spirit.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Whom to tell, and the body as God's temple — Practice
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Name three people you can report to if someone touches you inappropriately.

2. What number can a child in Kenya call free of charge for help?

3. What does 1 Corinthians 6:19 say about the body of a Christian?

## Answers to practice

1. Any three: a parent or guardian, a trusted grandparent, a teacher, a church leader, a police officer.

2. 116, Childline Kenya.

3. It is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and we are not our own.

## Summary
• Report bad touching to a parent, teacher, church leader or the police, and keep telling until you get help.
• Childline Kenya is 116.
• 1 Corinthians 6:19: your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, so live a holy life.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. In 2 Samuel 13, how did Amnon arrange for Tamar to come to him?
   A. He met her at the market
   B. He pretended to be ill so she would be sent to prepare food
   C. He wrote her a letter from another country
   D. He asked her in front of the whole town

2. What did Tamar do when Amnon asked her to lie with him?
   A. She agreed at once
   B. She said no and told him not to force her
   C. She called for a celebration
   D. She left the country before he spoke

3. Which action helps you take care when you are with a person of the opposite sex?
   A. Going into a closed bedroom alone
   B. Keeping the meeting secret from parents
   C. Staying where other people can see you
   D. Sending everyone else out of the room

4. Sexual abuse is...
   A. sometimes acceptable if the person is a relative
   B. always wrong
   C. the child's fault
   D. a game children should keep secret

5. Which of these protects you from sexual abuse?
   A. Accepting secret gifts
   B. Saying No and moving to where people are
   C. Keeping a bad secret
   D. Going to a lonely place

6. A bad secret is a secret that...

7. If someone touches you inappropriately, you should first:
   A. keep quiet forever
   B. tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher
   C. blame yourself
   D. hide from every adult

8. Which number is Childline Kenya?
   A. 116
   B. 100
   C. 123
   D. 911 only

9. 1 Corinthians 6:19 teaches that a Christian's body is:
   A. of no value
   B. a temple of the Holy Spirit
   C. belonging only to friends
   D. something to hide in shame

10. How can a learner live a holy life?

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. B. He pretended to be ill so she would be sent to prepare food
   Jonadab's plan was that Amnon should pretend to be ill and ask for Tamar to bring food.

2. B. She said no and told him not to force her
   Tamar refused and said the act was wicked. Amnon would not listen.

3. C. Staying where other people can see you
   Staying in view of other people is a way of taking care.

4. B. always wrong
   Sexual abuse is always wrong, and the blame belongs to the person who does it.

5. B. Saying No and moving to where people are
   A firm No and moving to other people are ways of protection.

6. hides harm and should be told to a trusted adult.
   Surprise gifts can be good secrets. Secrets about bad touching are not.

7. B. tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher
   Reporting to a responsible person brings help.

8. A. 116
   Children in Kenya can call 116 free of charge.

9. B. a temple of the Holy Spirit
   The verse says the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit and that we are not our own.

10. By saying no to sexual sin, respecting his or her body and other people's bodies, and asking God for help to stay pure.
   Holiness means being set apart for God, including keeping the body pure.
